changelog:
- Add optional per-user pause behavior overrides for multi-room mappings
- Leave pause behavior fields blank to inherit the global keep-colors or restore-light-state setting
- Apply effective per-user pause behavior during playback pause cleanup
- Add regression coverage for pause profile resolution, validation, persistence, lifecycle cleanup, and UI/API wiring
- Add optional per-user cinema-mode enablement and dim-level overrides for multi-room mappings
- Leave playback profile fields blank to inherit global cinema-mode settings
- Apply effective per-user cinema settings to startup dimming and cleanup restoration
- Add regression coverage for playback resolution, validation, persistence, cleanup, and UI/API wiring
- Add optional per-user color profiles for brightness boost, color saturation, hue shift, and output brightness
- Leave profile values blank to inherit global settings without changing existing mappings
- Resolve overrides live for each mapped playback user
- Add regression coverage for profile resolution, validation, persistence, API redaction, and UI wiring
- Add configurable -180 to 180 degree global hue shift for room-specific color correction or creative palettes
- Add regression coverage for hue wrapping, chromatic color rotation, validation, persistence, and UI/API wiring
- Apply hue rotation in HSL alongside saturation before final output brightness scaling
- Add configurable 0-100% final output brightness control independent of Brightness Boost
- Add regression coverage for output-brightness scaling, validation, persistence, and UI/API wiring
- Apply output brightness after boost and saturation so the ceiling dims without changing hue
- Add configurable Off, Auto, and On FFmpeg deinterlacing modes
- Report the active deinterlacing mode in Live Sync Status
- Add regression coverage for deinterlace filters, validation, persistence, and status
- Preserve Off as the default while Auto processes flagged interlaced frames and On forces deinterlacing
- Add configurable Stretch, Fit, and Crop video scaling modes
- Report the active video fit mode in Live Sync Status
- Add regression coverage for fit filters, validation, persistence, and status
- Preserve Stretch as the default while Fit and Crop handle non-16:9 source aspect ratios
- Add configurable 80x45, 160x90, and 320x180 RGB frame sampling resolutions
- Report the active frame resolution in Live Sync Status
- Add regression coverage for resolution validation, scaling, FFmpeg filters, and high-resolution sampling
- Use the selected frame resolution for FFmpeg output and spatial sampling while preserving the 160x90 default
- Add configurable Average, CenterWeighted, and CenterPixel spatial sampling modes
- Capture sampling mode per playback session while preserving Average behavior
- Add regression coverage for sampling modes, persistence, and color extraction
- Preserve the original playback-start light snapshot across same-session keep-colors pause/resume
- Restore saved light state before deactivating Hue output during service shutdown
- Add regression coverage for snapshot ownership and shutdown restoration
- Add configurable pause behavior to keep last synced colors or restore the original captured light state
- Report pause behavior in runtime status and preserve lifecycle ownership
- Add regression coverage for pause-time restoration and status
- Use Network Retry Attempts for both Hue REST retries and DTLS reconnect attempts
- Allow zero configured retries to disable DTLS reconnect attempts explicitly
- Add regression coverage for DTLS retry-attempt clamping and configuration wiring
- Add configurable 0-90% temporal color smoothing to reduce frame-to-frame flicker
- Clear smoothing history at blackout transitions so bright scenes recover immediately
- Add regression coverage for smoothing weights, initialization, and safe clamping
- Add configurable 1-50% color-sampling breadth around each Hue channel position
- Preserve the previous 15% sampling default while allowing fine-detail or noise-reduction tuning
- Add regression coverage for sampling validation, normalization, and scoped configuration persistence
- Keep stored per-user Hue credentials out of mapping read responses and the configuration-page settings flow
- Preserve existing per-user credentials when an administrator edits a mapping without entering replacement keys
- Add a scoped configuration API that updates default settings without round-tripping UserMappings
- Add regression coverage for credential redaction, safe mapping edits, and mapping preservation
- Preserve Hue color-temperature (mirek) state and restore the correct mode after playback
- Omit color payloads for lights that do not expose a color resource
- Add regression coverage for color, color-temperature, and colorless light restoration
- Recover automatically when FFmpeg stops producing video frames
- Add an administrator-configurable 1-60 second FFmpeg stall timeout with startup grace handling
- Surface stall diagnostics in Live Sync Status and restore/deactivate Hue state safely
- Add regression coverage for configured stall cleanup and diagnostics
- Roll back partially initialized sync sessions immediately when startup fails or is cancelled
- Dispose unowned FFmpeg streams and restore saved lights before waiting for playback stop
- Add regression coverage for startup restoration, area deactivation, ownership, and diagnostics
- Stop sync after repeated DTLS send failures instead of leaving lights frozen
- Restore saved light states and deactivate the entertainment area after send-failure exits
- Add regression coverage for bounded stream failure cleanup and error reporting
- Add automatic terminal cleanup when FFmpeg reaches EOF or the frame stream fails
- Restore saved light states and deactivate the entertainment area after terminal sync-loop exits
- Add regression coverage for EOF cleanup, failure cleanup, runtime ownership, and error preservation
- Add per-user sync opt-out controls for multi-user Jellyfin deployments
- Allow disabled user mappings to omit bridge credentials while preserving the default bridge for unmapped users
- Enforce per-user sync preferences before validation, FFmpeg startup, or Hue network calls
- Add regression coverage for disabled mappings, defaults, and runtime startup suppression
- Add a protected Stop Current Sync control that restores lights while playback continues
- Suppress automatic sync restarts for the manually stopped playback session until playback ends
- Report whether an administrator can stop the current sync session in runtime status
- Add lifecycle regression coverage for manual stop, stale stop notifications, and session suppression
- Add an optional non-destructive DTLS stream probe to Test Connection
- Verify the Hue Client Key and report whether a probe packet was written
- Add sanitized stream-probe result fields and regression coverage
- Add live runtime status and sanitized playback diagnostics to the API and configuration UI
- Show active bridge/area, frame count, sync duration, and FFmpeg/DTLS health while playback is running
- Add lifecycle regression coverage without exposing Hue credentials
- Add non-destructive bridge connection testing to the API and configuration UI
- Verify selected entertainment areas contain controllable channels
- Add explicit edit and cancel controls for per-user bridge mappings
- Load entertainment areas through a body-based API so Hue app keys are not sent in URLs
- Keep the legacy GET area endpoint available for existing clients
- Add authenticated bridge discovery to the configuration API and UI
- Add one-click discovery for default and per-user bridge mappings
- Keep plugin JSON and encoding dependencies on the .NET 8 servicing line
- Pin vulnerable legacy transitive framework packages to safe compatible versions
- Use the Hue bridge HTTPS API for link-button registration on current firmware
- Scope local certificate handling to private bridge addresses
- Require bridge targets to be private/local addresses or .local mDNS names
- Hardened playback lifecycle cleanup across stop, pause, resume, and shutdown events
- Added transient Hue bridge HTTP retries and malformed-response handling
- Improved FFmpeg and DTLS process ownership and reconnect safety
- Added validation for per-user bridge mappings and stream packet inputs
- Updated release packaging and documentation
description: Synchronize Philips Hue lights with your media playback in real-time.
name: Philips Hue Sync
overview: Adds support for real-time lighting synchronization with Philips Hue Entertainment Areas using the streaming DTLS API. Features cinema mode, scene restoration, per-user bridge mappings, advanced color processing, and auto-reconnection.
